samuel1.13.p1.b1.text: Saul was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned over Israel forty-two years. He chose for himself three thousand men of Israel …

samuel1.13.p1.b2.text: Then Jonathan attacked the Philistine outpost at Geba, and the Philistines heard about it.

samuel1.13.p1.b3.text: So Saul blew the ram’s horn throughout the land, saying, “Let the Hebrews hear!”

samuel1.13.p1.b4.text: And all Israel heard the news … Then the people were summoned to join Saul at Gilgal.

samuel1.13.p2.b1.text: Now the Philistines assembled to fight against Israel with three thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen, and troops as numerous as the sand on the seashore …

samuel1.13.p2.b2.text: Seeing that they were in danger because their troops were hard-pressed, the men of Israel hid in caves and thickets, among the rocks, and in cellars and cisterns.

samuel1.13.p2.b3.text: Some Hebrews even crossed the Jordan into the land of Gad and Gilead.

samuel1.13.p2.b4.text: Saul, however, remained at Gilgal, and all his troops were quaking in fear.

samuel1.13.p3.b1.text: And Saul waited seven days for the time appointed by Samuel

samuel1.13.p3.b2.text: but Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the troops began to desert Saul.

samuel1.13.p3.b3.text: Bring me the burnt offering and the peace offerings.

samuel1.13.p4.b1.text: Just as he finished offering the burnt offering, Samuel arrived, and Saul went out to greet him.

samuel1.13.p4.b3.text: When I saw that the troops were deserting me, and that you did not come at the appointed time … So I felt compelled to offer the burnt offering.

samuel1.13.p5.b1.text: You have acted foolishly … You have not kept the command that the LORD your God gave you

samuel1.13.p5.b2.text: if you had, the LORD would have established your kingdom over Israel for all time. But now your kingdom will not endure

samuel1.13.p5.b3.text: the LORD has sought a man after His own heart and appointed him ruler over His people …

samuel1.13.p5.b4.text: Then Samuel set out from Gilgal and went up to Gibeah in Benjamin. And Saul numbered the troops who were with him, about six hundred men.

samuel1.13.p6.b1.text: Now Saul and Jonathan his son and the troops with them were staying in Geba of Benjamin, while the Philistines camped at Michmash.

samuel1.13.p6.b2.text: And raiders went out of the Philistine camp in three divisions. One headed toward Ophrah in the land of Shual …

samuel1.13.p7.b1.text: And no blacksmith could be found in all the land of Israel, because the Philistines had said, “The Hebrews must not be allowed to make swords or spears.”

samuel1.13.p7.b2.text: Instead, all the Israelites would go down to the Philistines to sharpen their plowshares, mattocks, axes, and sickles.

samuel1.13.p7.b3.text: So on the day of battle not a sword or spear could be found in the hands of the troops with Saul and Jonathan; only Saul and his son Jonathan had weapons.

samuel1.13.p7.b4.text: And a garrison of the Philistines had gone out to the pass at Michmash.
